blocks.text: For Ilocano communities across Northern and Central Luzon, mourning does not end with burial. A day after accompanying their departed loved one to their final resting place, bereaved families make their way to a river or the sea to take part in an age-old ritual known as gulgol. “From the provinces of the Ilocos Region to the diasporic Ilocano communities…people practice ‘gulgol’ as part of their mourning rituals,” Aldous Tracy Rubio, an anthropologist pursuing a Master of Arts in History at the University of the Philippines Baguio, told the Inquirer.
